_about: Hand-written. Sorts each query before any verse is chosen (search/FORMAT.md step 3). 'crisis': no verses, no themes, no notes; the site shows 'crisis_message' (no phone numbers, by the owner's decision). Two layers fire it: the 'crisis' phrase lists (suicide, self-harm, abuse, harm to others) and the deliberately over-sensitive 'distress' gate, whose rules fire when a few words occur close together in any order ('pills' near 'how many', 'he' near 'grabs me', 'better off' near 'without me'); when in doubt it fires. Before either is matched, the words of every 'idioms' phrase ('killing it at work', 'cut back on sugar') and every 'bereavement' phrase (a third person's death: 'my dad passed away', 'died by suicide', 'lost my brother to an overdose') are blanked, and a word of 5+ letters one edit away from a 'fuzzy' word is read as that word ('suicdie' -> 'suicide'). Bereavement thus reaches the grief theme, while anything else in the message ('and i want to die too') is still read. 'sensitive': identity, body, health and life-circumstance topics; only verses of search/pool/sensitive_set.json can be returned, with the topic's gentle themes added after any themes the visitor typed. Phrases use the syntax of search/themes.json; distress rules are described in search/FORMAT.md. The lists were developed against the probe sets in evals/search_probes.json and are tested in both directions. 'suggest' (round 7, used only by suggest()): if a message has any of the 'signals' (first-person harm, a plan, secrecy, an age under 18, contact with an adult or a stranger), the topics in 'never_after_signal' are never offered and at most 'max_topics_after_signal' topics are, even if the gate did not fire. 'emoji' maps a few emoji to words before the crisis words are read ('🔫' -> 'emojigun').
